items.stem: Before refactoring a complex, untested legacy function, the safest first step is to:

options.text: Add characterisation tests that capture current behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: capturing existing behaviour lets you refactor without changing it unknowingly.
Rewriting without a safety net risks silent behaviour changes.

options.text: Delete it and see what breaks
options.rationale: Removing code to probe dependencies is reckless in production code.
Renaming does not protect behaviour during a refactor.

items.explanation: Correct: capturing existing behaviour lets you refactor without changing it unknowingly.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO make a large refactor reviewable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Splitting it into small, ordered steps
options.rationale: Correct: small steps are far easier to review correctly.

options.text: Keeping each step building and passing tests
options.rationale: Correct: green intermediate states keep the refactor recoverable.

options.text: Bundling unrelated feature changes to save a PR
options.rationale: Mixing changes obscures review and raises risk.

options.text: Avoiding tests so the diff is smaller
options.rationale: Dropping tests removes the safety net the refactor needs.

items.explanation: Correct: small steps are far easier to review correctly.

items.stem: An audit lists twenty findings. What should drive which to fix first?

options.text: Their impact weighed against the effort to fix them
Which one is quickest to fix regardless of impact
options.rationale: Easiest-first can leave the biggest risks untouched.
File name order has no bearing on risk.

options.text: Which the newest team member prefers
options.rationale: Preference is not a prioritisation basis for risk.
